content.content:
Доски и спринты - **`boards_get_all`**: Получить Agile-доски, доступные в организации - Параметры: - `queue` (строка, опционально): Вернуть только доски, которые собирают задачи этой очереди, например `"SOMEPROJECT"` - `fields` (массив строк, опционально): Поля, которые нужно вернуть. Выбор `["id", "name"]` при поиске доски уменьшает ответ примерно в 30 раз - `page` (целое число, опционально, по умолчанию 1): Номер страницы - `per_page` (целое число, опционально, по умолчанию 50): Количество элементов на странице - Возвращает список досок с id, названием, версией, колонками, настройками и метаданными создания - **Как найти доску проекта**: у доски нет собственного поля с очередью — она собирает то, что подходит под её `autoFilterSettings`, поэтому `queue` сопоставляется именно с этим фильтром. Серверной фильтрации у Трекера здесь нет, поэтому инструмент читает весь список и фильтрует локально. Регистр не важен, доска с несколькими очередями находится по любой из них, а инвертированное условие («очередь не X») совпадением не считается. Доски, в фильтре которых очередь не указана вовсе, найти этим способом нельзя, и при заданном `queue` они не попадают в результат; сколько их — целиком зависит от того, как настроены доски в конкретной организации. Чтобы найти и их, прочитайте несколько задач очереди через `issues_find` и посмотрите на их поле `boards`: Трекер заполняет его по фильтрам самих досок, поэтому персональная доска, собирающая задачи одного исполнителя, там видна, даже если очередь в её фильтре не указана. - `queue` учитывает `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES`: обращение к запрещённой очереди отклоняется - Используйте полученный `id` доски в инструментах `board_get`, `board_get_columns` и `board_get_sprints` - У `GET /v3/boards` нет собственной постраничной навигации, он отдаёт сразу все доски организации, поэтому инструмент разбивает результат на страницы сам: в организации с сотнями досок один вызов иначе вернул бы четверть мегабайта JSON. Увеличивайте `page`, пока результат не станет пустым. - Доски относятся ко всей организации, поэтому не фильтруются настройкой `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` - **`board_get`**: Получить одну Agile-доску с её настройками - Параметры: - `board_id` (целое число, идентификатор доски из `boards_get_all`) - `fields` (массив строк, опционально): Поля, которые нужно вернуть - `autoFilterSettings` — это собственный фильтр доски: он говорит, какие задачи доска собирает, поэтому именно по нему видно, про какую очередь доска. `addFilterSettings` описывает, что попадает на доску, `removeFilterSettings` — что с неё уходит; условие задаётся либо фиксированным значением (очередь, тип задачи), либо макросом вроде `empty()` / `notEmpty()` - Также возвращает `estimateBy` (поле, по которому оценивают задачи), `useRanking` и производственный `calendar`, по которому считаются рабочие дни спринта - Несуществующий `board_id` возвращается как ошибка «доска не найдена» - **`board_get_columns`**: Получить колонки Agile-доски вместе со статусами задач - Параметры: `board_id` (целое число, идентификатор доски из `boards_get_all`) - Возвращает каждую колонку с `id`, `name` и списком статусов задач `statuses`, которые в неё попадают — по нему видно, в какой статус нужно перевести задачу, чтобы она оказалась в нужной колонке - Богаче, чем колонки внутри `boards_get_all` / `board_get`: там статусов нет - **`board_get_sprints`**: Получить все спринты конкретной Agile-доски - Параметры: - `board_id` (целое число, идентификатор доски из `boards_get_all`) - `fields` (массив строк, опционально): Поля, которые нужно вернуть - У доски, которая не является scrum-доской, спринтов нет, и API отклоняет вызов с сообщением «У доски этого типа не может быть спринтов.»; несуществующий `board_id` возвращается как ошибка «доска не найдена» - Возвращает список спринтов с id, названием, статусом, признаком архивности, плановыми датами (`startDate`, `endDate`) и фактическими датами (`startDateTime`, `endDateTime`) - Статус спринта — одно из значений `draft`, `in_progress`, `released` или `archived`; текущий спринт — тот, у которого статус `in_progress` - Используйте полученный `id` спринта, чтобы поместить задачу в спринт с помощью `issue_create` или `issue_update` У задачи, полученной через `issue_get` / `issues_find`, есть поле `boards` со списком досок, на которых она отображается (`{"id": 2, "name": "..."}`) — этот `id` можно сразу передавать в инструменты выше. Трекер заполняет `boards` по фильтрам самих досок, поэтому поле только для чтения: задачу нельзя назначить на доску напрямую, она просто попадает под её фильтр.

53:- **`GET /v3/boards` does not paginate.** `page` / `perPage` are ignored and every board of the organization comes back in one response (404 boards / ~250 KB on a real org), so `boards_get_all` pages the list itself and takes `fields`. Any new board listing has to bound its own output the same way.
54-- **A board has no queue field.** What lands on it is whatever `autoFilterSettings` matches, so "boards of queue X" is answered by reading the queue out of that filter (`board_queue_keys()` in `mcp/tools/board.py`), and `?queue=` on the endpoint is ignored like the paging parameters. Boards whose filter names no queue cannot be found this way at all, and how many of those exist depends on how an organization sets its boards up (it was a third of them on the organization this was checked against) - so a queue-scoped listing has to say it may be incomplete rather than imply the queue has no other boards. The second route covers them: an issue's `boards` is filled in by Tracker from the boards' own filters, so reading a few issues of the queue surfaces the personal and assignee-filtered boards that `queue` cannot match (verified: `DEVOPSOBR` matches 2 boards by filter and 6 through its issues). The server `instructions` tell agents to try both.
55-- **Board settings live on the board record**, not on a sub-resource: `autoFilterSettings` (the board's filter - which issues it collects), `estimateBy`, `useRanking`, `country`, `calendar`. `/v3/boards/{id}/filter` and `/settings` do not exist. `autoFilterSettings` is present in the *listing* too, which is why `fields` matters there.
56-- **A filter condition is not always a reference.** `autoFilterSettings.…​.liveFilter.fieldValues[].value[]` carries either `fixed` (an object for most fields, but a bare string for enumerated ones like `statusType`) or `macro` (`empty()` / `notEmpty()`), so `fixed` is typed `BoardFilterValueRef | str | None`. `filterFieldsOrder` repeats the same fields for display order and is deliberately not modelled.

feat: page boards_get_all like the other listings, and own up to the allow-list

Two review decisions, both about what `boards_get_all` promises.

`{values, hits, pages}`. 90c0a18 moved every listing onto the envelope
while this branch was out, and boards answered with a bare list. They no
longer do. The envelope also gives this tool something the others cannot
have: `GET /v3/boards` hands over the whole organization in one response,
so `hits` / `pages` are counted here rather than read off a page Tracker
reported, and are exact. `page` stays 1 by default where the other
listings default to None and walk themselves - the walk costs one request
and a quarter of a megabyte of the caller's context, so it is the escape
hatch (`page: null`, meant to be paired with a narrow `fields`) rather
than the default. `per_page` drops 50 -> 25: a full board record carries
`autoFilterSettings` and its columns, so a page of them is not cheap.

Boards stay outside `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES`. Filtering them by the queues
in their own auto-filter was the other option, and it takes away what the
tools are for - a board has no queue, "the boards of queue X" is already
a best-effort match on a filter, and half an organization's boards name
no queue at all. So the leak is documented instead of coded around: a
board's settings can name a queue the rest of the server refuses to talk
about, `board_get` and friends answer for any board id, and on a
deployment where the allow-list is the only boundary those keys and
display names are exposed. Both READMEs say so where the board tools are
described and again where an operator reads about the allow-list, which
also settles the two adjacent lines that contradicted each other.

"""Board and sprint MCP tools (read-only)."""

import math
from typing import Annotated, Any

from mcp.server import FastMCP
from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context
from mcp.types import ToolAnnotations
from pydantic import Field

from mcp_tracker.mcp.context import AppContext
from mcp_tracker.mcp.params import (
    BoardID,
    BoardPageParam,
    BoardQueueFilter,
    PerPageParam,
)
from mcp_tracker.mcp.tools._access import check_queue_access
from mcp_tracker.mcp.utils import get_yandex_auth, set_non_needed_fields_null
from mcp_tracker.settings import Settings
from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types.boards import (
    Board,
    BoardColumnDetail,
    BoardFieldsEnum,
    Sprint,
    SprintFieldsEnum,
)
from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types.pagination import PaginatedResult

BoardFieldsParam = Annotated[
    list[BoardFieldsEnum] | None,
    Field(
        description="Fields to include in the response. In order to not pollute the "
        "context window - select appropriate fields beforehand. Not specifying fields "
        "will return all available. When looking for a board, id and name are usually "
        "enough; read the full record of the one board you need with `board_get`.",
    ),
]

SprintFieldsParam = Annotated[
    list[SprintFieldsEnum] | None,
    Field(
        description="Fields to include in the response. In order to not pollute the "
        "context window - select appropriate fields beforehand. Not specifying fields "
        "will return all available. Most of the time id, name and status are enough.",
    ),
]


def board_queue_keys(board: Board) -> set[str]:
    """Queue keys a board collects issues from, read off its own auto-filter.

    A board carries no queue field: what lands on it is whatever
    `addFilterSettings` matches, so the queue has to be read out of that filter.
    An inverted condition ("queue is not X") says which queue the board is
    *not* about and is therefore not a match.
    """
    settings = board.autoFilterSettings
    add = settings.addFilterSettings if settings is not None else None
    live = add.liveFilter if add is not None else None
    if live is None or live.fieldValues is None:
        return set()

    keys: set[str] = set()
    for field in live.fieldValues:
        if field.id != "queue" or field.value is None:
            continue
        for value in field.value:
            fixed = value.fixed
            if value.invert or fixed is None or isinstance(fixed, str):
                continue
            if fixed.key is not None:
                keys.add(fixed.key.upper())

    return keys


def register_board_tools(settings: Settings, mcp: FastMCP[Any]) -> None:
    """Register board and sprint tools (all read-only)."""

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get All Boards",
        description="Get the agile boards (in russian - 'доски') available in Yandex Tracker. "
        "Use the returned board id with the `board_get`, `board_get_columns` and "
        "`board_get_sprints` tools. "
        "Pass `queue` to get only the boards that collect issues of that queue - "
        "that is the way to answer 'which board does this project use'. It matches "
        "the board's own filter, so it misses boards filtering by something else "
        "(personal boards, for one); to catch those, read a few issues of the queue "
        "with `issues_find` and look at their `boards` field. "
        "An organization can have hundreds of boards, so the listing is paginated - "
        "the answer carries `hits` and `pages`, and page 1 is the default. Pass "
        "`fields` to keep the answer small while searching for the board you need. "
        "Boards are organization-wide and are NOT filtered by the server's queue "
        "allow-list: a board's settings can name a queue this server otherwise "
        "refuses to talk about.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def boards_get_all(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        queue: BoardQueueFilter = None,
        fields: BoardFieldsParam = None,
        page: BoardPageParam = 1,
        per_page: PerPageParam = 25,
    ) -> PaginatedResult[Board]:
        if queue is not None:
            check_queue_access(settings, queue)

        boards = await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.boards_list(
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

        # Tracker has no server-side filter here (`?queue=` is ignored along with
        # `page` / `perPage`), so the queue is matched against each board's own
        # auto-filter. Filtering runs before paging, or `page` would count boards
        # that are then dropped.
        if queue is not None:
            wanted = queue.upper()
            boards = [b for b in boards if wanted in board_queue_keys(b)]

        # `GET /v3/boards` ignores `page` / `perPage` and always answers with every
        # board, so the paging has to happen here. Left unbounded the tool returns
        # a quarter of a megabyte of JSON on a real organization, which is enough
        # to exhaust the caller's context on a single call - hence a page by
        # default, where the other listings walk themselves.
        if page is None:
            result = PaginatedResult[Board](values=boards)
        else:
            start = (page - 1) * per_page
            # The whole listing is in hand, so unlike the tools paging against
            # Tracker these totals are exact rather than whatever the last page
            # happened to report.
            result = PaginatedResult[Board](
                values=boards[start : start + per_page],
                hits=len(boards),
                pages=math.ceil(len(boards) / per_page),
            )

        if fields is not None:
            set_non_needed_fields_null(result.values, {f.name for f in fields})

        return result

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get Board",
        description="Get a single Yandex Tracker agile board (in russian - 'доска') "
        "with its settings. `autoFilterSettings` is the board's own filter and tells "
        "which issues the board collects - read it to learn which queue a board is about. "
        "Also returns the columns, the field issues are estimated by and the working "
        "calendar the board uses.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def board_get(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        board_id: BoardID,
        fields: BoardFieldsParam = None,
    ) -> Board:
        board = await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.board_get(
            board_id,
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

        if fields is not None:
            set_non_needed_fields_null([board], {f.name for f in fields})

        return board

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get Board Columns",
        description="Get the columns of a Yandex Tracker agile board together with the "
        "issue statuses mapped onto each of them. Use it to find out which status an "
        "issue has to be in to show up in a given column of the board. "
        "Richer than the columns nested in `boards_get_all` / `board_get`, which carry "
        "no statuses.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def board_get_columns(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        board_id: BoardID,
    ) -> list[BoardColumnDetail]:
        return await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.board_get_columns(
            board_id,
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get Board Sprints",
        description="Get all sprints (in russian - 'спринты') of a specific Yandex Tracker agile board. "
        "The currently running sprint is the one with status 'in_progress'. "
        "Use the returned sprint id to put an issue into a sprint "
        "with the `issue_create` or `issue_update` tools.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def board_get_sprints(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        board_id: BoardID,
        fields: SprintFieldsParam = None,
    ) -> list[Sprint]:
        sprints = await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.board_get_sprints(
            board_id,
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

        if fields is not None:
            set_non_needed_fields_null(sprints, {f.name for f in fields})

        return sprints

        "context window - select appropriate fields beforehand. Not specifying fields "
        "will return all available. Most of the time id, name and status are enough.",
    ),
]


def board_queue_keys(board: Board) -> set[str]:
    """Queue keys a board collects issues from, read off its own auto-filter.

    A board carries no queue field: what lands on it is whatever
    `addFilterSettings` matches, so the queue has to be read out of that filter.
    An inverted condition ("queue is not X") says which queue the board is
    *not* about and is therefore not a match.
    """
    settings = board.autoFilterSettings
    add = settings.addFilterSettings if settings is not None else None
    live = add.liveFilter if add is not None else None
    if live is None or live.fieldValues is None:
        return set()

    keys: set[str] = set()
    for field in live.fieldValues:
        # The captured payloads name this field twice, `id` and `key`, so
        # matching on both keeps this working whichever one a response carries.
        if "queue" not in (field.id, field.key) or field.value is None:
            continue
        for value in field.value:
            fixed = value.fixed
            if value.invert or fixed is None or isinstance(fixed, str):
                continue
            if fixed.key is not None:
                keys.add(fixed.key.upper())

    return keys


def register_board_tools(settings: Settings, mcp: FastMCP[Any]) -> None:
    """Register board and sprint tools (all read-only)."""

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get All Boards",
        description="Get the agile boards (in russian - 'доски') available in Yandex Tracker. "
        "Use the returned board id with the `board_get`, `board_get_columns` and "
        "`board_get_sprints` tools. "
        "Pass `queue` to get only the boards that collect issues of that queue - "
        "that is the way to answer 'which board does this project use'. It matches "
        "the board's own filter, so it misses boards filtering by something else "
        "(personal boards, for one); to catch those, read a few issues of the queue "
        "with `issues_find` and look at their `boards` field. "
        "An organization can have hundreds of boards, so the listing is paginated - "
        "the answer carries `hits` and `pages`, and page 1 is the default. Pass "
        "`fields` to keep the answer small while searching for the board you need. "
        "Boards are organization-wide and are NOT filtered by the server's queue "
        "allow-list: a board's settings can name a queue this server otherwise "
        "refuses to talk about.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def boards_get_all(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        queue: BoardQueueFilter = None,
        fields: BoardFieldsParam = None,
        page: BoardPageParam = 1,
        per_page: PerPageParam = 25,
    ) -> PaginatedResult[Board]:
        if queue is not None:
            check_queue_access(settings, queue)

        boards = await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.boards_list(
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

        # Tracker has no server-side filter here (`?queue=` is ignored along with
        # `page` / `perPage`), so the queue is matched against each board's own
        # auto-filter. Filtering runs before paging, or `page` would count boards
        # that are then dropped.
        if queue is not None:
            wanted = queue.upper()
            boards = [b for b in boards if wanted in board_queue_keys(b)]

        # `GET /v3/boards` ignores `page` / `perPage` and always answers with every
        # board, so the paging has to happen here. Left unbounded the tool returns
        # a quarter of a megabyte of JSON on a real organization, which is enough
        # to exhaust the caller's context on a single call - hence a page by
        # default, where the other listings walk themselves.
        if page is None:
            result = PaginatedResult[Board](values=boards)
        else:
            start = (page - 1) * per_page
            # The whole listing is in hand, so unlike the tools paging against
            # Tracker these totals are exact rather than whatever the last page
            # happened to report.
            result = PaginatedResult[Board](
                values=boards[start : start + per_page],
                hits=len(boards),
                pages=math.ceil(len(boards) / per_page),
            )

        if fields is not None:
            set_non_needed_fields_null(result.values, {f.name for f in fields})

        return result

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get Board",
        description="Get a single Yandex Tracker agile board (in russian - 'доска') "
        "with its settings. `autoFilterSettings` is the board's own filter and tells "
        "which issues the board collects - read it to learn which queue a board is about. "
        "Also returns the columns, the field issues are estimated by and the working "
        "calendar the board uses.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def board_get(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        board_id: BoardID,
        fields: BoardFieldsParam = None,
    ) -> Board:
        board = await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.board_get(
            board_id,
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

        if fields is not None:
            set_non_needed_fields_null([board], {f.name for f in fields})

        return board

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get Board Columns",
        description="Get the columns of a Yandex Tracker agile board together with the "
        "issue statuses mapped onto each of them. Use it to find out which status an "
        "issue has to be in to show up in a given column of the board. "
        "Richer than the columns nested in `boards_get_all` / `board_get`, which carry "
        "no statuses.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def board_get_columns(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        board_id: BoardID,
    ) -> list[BoardColumnDetail]:
        return await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.board_get_columns(
            board_id,
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get Board Sprints",
        description="Get all sprints (in russian - 'спринты') of a specific Yandex Tracker agile board. "
        "The currently running sprint is the one with status 'in_progress'. "
        "Use the returned sprint id to put an issue into a sprint "
        "with the `issue_create` or `issue_update` tools.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def board_get_sprints(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        board_id: BoardID,
        fields: SprintFieldsParam = None,
    ) -> list[Sprint]:
        sprints = await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.board_get_sprints(
            board_id,
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

        if fields is not None:
            set_non_needed_fields_null(sprints, {f.name for f in fields})

        return sprints

import datetime
from enum import Enum

from pydantic import Field

from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types.base import (
    BaseTrackerEntity,
    NoneExcludedField,
    none_excluder,
)
from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types.refs import (
    BaseReference,
    BoardReference,
    UserReference,
)
from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types.statuses import Status


class BoardColumn(BaseReference):
    """A column of an agile board, as nested in a board record."""

    display: str | None = None


class BoardColumnStatus(BaseReference):
    """An issue status that lands in a board column."""

    key: str | None = Field(
        None, exclude_if=none_excluder, description="Status key, e.g. 'inProgress'"
    )
    display: str | None = Field(
        None, exclude_if=none_excluder, description="Displayed status name"
    )


class BoardColumnDetail(BaseTrackerEntity):
    """A column of an agile board with the statuses mapped onto it.

    `GET /v3/boards/{id}/columns` answers with more than the columns nested in
    a board record: it says which issue statuses land in which column, and it
    spells the column out as `id` (a number) / `name` rather than the nested
    form's `id` (a string) / `display`.
    """

    id: int | None = Field(
        None, exclude_if=none_excluder, description="Column identifier"
    )
    name: str | None = NoneExcludedField
    statuses: list[BoardColumnStatus] | None = Field(
        None,
        exclude_if=none_excluder,
        description="Issue statuses shown in this column",
    )


class BoardFilterValueRef(BaseReference):
    """A value referenced by a board filter: a queue, an issue type, a user, ..."""

    key: str | None = Field(
        None, exclude_if=none_excluder, description="Key of the referenced entity"
    )
    display: str | None = Field(
        None, exclude_if=none_excluder, description="Human-readable name"
    )


class BoardFilterFieldValue(BaseTrackerEntity):
    """One value a board's auto-filter matches on.

    A condition is either a concrete value (`fixed`) or a macro (`macro`), so a
    board that collects "issues with no resolution" carries `empty()` here and
    no `fixed` at all. `fixed` is a reference object for most fields but a bare
    string for the enumerated ones such as `statusType`.
    """

    fixed: BoardFilterValueRef | str | None = Field(
        None,
        exclude_if=none_excluder,
        description="The matched value, e.g. a queue or an issue type",
    )
    macro: str | None = Field(
        None,
        exclude_if=none_excluder,
        description="Condition applied instead of a fixed value: "
        "'empty()' or 'notEmpty()'",
    )
    invert: bool | None = Field(
        None,
        exclude_if=none_excluder,
        description="True when the condition is negated ('is not')",
    )


class BoardFilterField(BaseTrackerEntity):
    """A field a board's auto-filter matches on, with the values it accepts."""

    id: str | None = NoneExcludedField
    key: str | None = NoneExcludedField
    name: str | None = NoneExcludedField
    display: str | None = NoneExcludedField
    fieldType: str | None = NoneExcludedField
    value: list[BoardFilterFieldValue] | None = Field(
        None, exclude_if=none_excluder, description="Accepted values of this field"
    )


class BoardLiveFilter(BaseTrackerEntity):
    """The field conditions of a board's auto-filter.

    Tracker repeats the same fields under `filterFieldsOrder` to record their
    display order; that is a UI detail and `extra="ignore"` drops it, together
    with the field metadata (`schema`, `qlFieldType`, `fullLocalization`, ...)
    that `queue_get_fields` already describes.
    """

    fieldValues: list[BoardFilterField] | None = Field(
        None, exclude_if=none_excluder, description="Conditions an issue has to match"
    )


class BoardFilterSettings(BaseTrackerEntity):
    """One half of a board's auto-filter: what puts issues on it, or takes them off."""

    liveFilter: BoardLiveFilter | None = NoneExcludedField
    statuses: list[Status] | None = Field(
        None,
        exclude_if=none_excluder,
        description="Issue statuses this rule applies to",
    )
    checkResolutionPresence: bool | None = NoneExcludedField
    maxTimeInToRemoveState: str | None = Field(
        None,
        exclude_if=none_excluder,
        description="How long an issue stays before the rule fires, as an ISO-8601 "
        "duration (e.g. 'P2W' for two weeks)",
    )
    enabled: bool | None = NoneExcludedField


class BoardAutoFilterSettings(BaseTrackerEntity):
    """Which issues a board picks up automatically, and which it drops.

    This is the closest thing a board has to a query: `addFilterSettings`
    describes what lands on the board (usually a queue, sometimes narrowed by
    issue type or status), `removeFilterSettings` what leaves it.
    """

    addFilterSettings: BoardFilterSettings | None = NoneExcludedField
    removeFilterSettings: BoardFilterSettings | None = NoneExcludedField
    addActionSettings: BoardFilterSettings | None = NoneExcludedField
    removeActionSettings: BoardFilterSettings | None = NoneExcludedField


class Board(BaseTrackerEntity):
    """An agile board ("доска задач") of the organization."""

    # `fields` projection nulls out what the caller did not ask for, so an id
    # that stays required would leave `"id": null` against a schema saying int.
    id: int | None = Field(
        None, exclude_if=none_excluder, description="Board identifier"
    )
    version: int | None = NoneExcludedField
    name: str | None = NoneExcludedField
    createdAt: datetime.datetime | None = NoneExcludedField
    updatedAt: datetime.datetime | None = NoneExcludedField
    createdBy: UserReference | None = NoneExcludedField
    columns: list[BoardColumn] | None = NoneExcludedField
    autoFilterSettings: BoardAutoFilterSettings | None = Field(

        description="Which issues the board picks up automatically. This is the "

    )
    estimateBy: BoardFilterValueRef | None = Field(

        exclude_if=none_excluder,
        description="Field the board estimates issues by, e.g. 'storyPoints'",
    )
    useRanking: bool | None = Field(

        exclude_if=none_excluder,
        description="Whether issues are ordered by manual ranking",
    )
    country: BoardFilterValueRef | None = Field(
        None,
        exclude_if=none_excluder,
        description="Country whose working calendar the board uses",
    )
    calendar: BaseReference | None = Field(
        None,
        exclude_if=none_excluder,
        description="Working calendar used to count working days in a sprint",
    )


class Sprint(BaseTrackerEntity):
    """A sprint of an agile board."""

    id: int | None = Field(
        None, exclude_if=none_excluder, description="Sprint identifier"
    )
    version: int | None = NoneExcludedField
    name: str | None = NoneExcludedField
    board: BoardReference | None = NoneExcludedField
    status: str | None = Field(
        None,
        exclude_if=none_excluder,
        description="Sprint status: 'draft' (open), 'in_progress' (the currently "

    )
    archived: bool | None = NoneExcludedField
    createdAt: datetime.datetime | None = NoneExcludedField
    createdBy: UserReference | None = NoneExcludedField
    startDate: datetime.date | None = Field(
        None, exclude_if=none_excluder, description="Planned sprint start date"
    )
    endDate: datetime.date | None = Field(
        None, exclude_if=none_excluder, description="Planned sprint end date"
    )
    startDateTime: datetime.datetime | None = Field(
        None, exclude_if=none_excluder, description="Actual sprint start date and time"
    )
    endDateTime: datetime.datetime | None = Field(
        None, exclude_if=none_excluder, description="Actual sprint end date and time"
    )


BoardFieldsEnum = Enum(  # type: ignore[misc]

fix: the four minor findings from the board review

**The allow-list check ignored the case the match honours.** `queue` was
upper-cased for matching a board's filter and passed raw to
`check_queue_access`, so `queue="levelarm"` walked past the allow-list and
then answered for `LEVELARM`, while `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES=LEVELARM` rejected
the same call as "not found or not allowed". Normalised once, before the
check. A lower-cased allow-list entry now stops matching here, which is
what it already does everywhere else - `check_issue_access` reads the key
off the issue id and compares it as-is.

**The queue field of a filter was recognised by `id` alone.** Captured
payloads name it twice, `id` and `key`; either is enough now.

**`Sprint.board.id` arrives as a string** while `BoardID` is an `int`.
`BaseReference.id` is `Any`, so the schema cannot say this - the field
description does, for the agent walking sprint -> board.

**`BoardNotFound` had no test above the client.** Three client-level tests
covered the raising; nothing covered the error reaching the caller as
`isError` rather than as an empty answer it would then reason from. One
parametrized test over the three board-scoped tools.

Отдельным коммитом `614eebc`. `task` зелёный: **1361 passed, 1 skipped** (+10 тестов).

**Регистр (`board.py:108`).** `wanted = queue.upper()` теперь считается один раз и идёт и в `check_queue_access`, и в матч. Побочный эффект, который стоит знать: очередь, записанная в `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` строчными, теперь на досках перестаёт совпадать — но она и так не работает нигде больше, `check_issue_access` берёт ключ из id задачи как есть. Тесты `test_restricted_queue_is_rejected` / `test_permitted_queue_is_allowed` параметризованы по трём регистрам.

"""Unit tests for the access-control helpers in ``mcp/tools/_access.py``."""

import pytest

from mcp_tracker.mcp.errors import TrackerError
from mcp_tracker.mcp.tools._access import check_issue_access, check_queue_access
from mcp_tracker.settings import Settings
from mcp_tracker.tracker.custom.errors import IssueNotFound
from tests.mcp.conftest import create_test_settings


class TestCheckIssueAccess:
    def test_no_restrictions_allows_read_and_write(self) -> None:
        settings = create_test_settings()

        # Should not raise for either read or write.
        check_issue_access(settings, "TEST-1")
        check_issue_access(settings, "TEST-1", write=True)

    def test_read_only_queue_allows_reads(self) -> None:
        settings = create_test_settings(read_only_queues=["READONLY"])

        # Read access to a read-only queue is permitted.
        check_issue_access(settings, "READONLY-1")

    def test_read_only_queue_rejects_writes(self) -> None:
        settings = create_test_settings(read_only_queues=["READONLY"])

        with pytest.raises(TrackerError, match="read-only"):
            check_issue_access(settings, "READONLY-1", write=True)

    def test_writable_queue_allows_writes(self) -> None:
        settings = create_test_settings(read_only_queues=["READONLY"])

        # A queue not in the read-only list stays writable.
        check_issue_access(settings, "TEST-1", write=True)

    def test_limit_queues_takes_precedence(self) -> None:
        settings = create_test_settings(
            limit_queues=["ALLOWED"], read_only_queues=["READONLY"]
        )

        # A queue outside the allow-list is not found, even for reads.
        with pytest.raises(IssueNotFound):
            check_issue_access(settings, "OTHER-1")

    def test_limit_and_read_only_combined(self) -> None:
        settings = create_test_settings(
            limit_queues=["ALLOWED", "READONLY"], read_only_queues=["READONLY"]
        )

        # Allowed + writable queue: read and write both fine.
        check_issue_access(settings, "ALLOWED-1", write=True)
        # Allowed but read-only queue: reads fine, writes rejected.
        check_issue_access(settings, "READONLY-1")
        with pytest.raises(TrackerError, match="read-only"):
            check_issue_access(settings, "READONLY-1", write=True)

"""Access control helpers for MCP tools."""

from mcp_tracker.mcp.errors import TrackerError
from mcp_tracker.settings import Settings
from mcp_tracker.tracker.custom.errors import IssueNotFound


def _is_read_only_queue(settings: Settings, queue: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if the given queue is configured as read-only."""
    return bool(
        settings.tracker_read_only_queues and queue in settings.tracker_read_only_queues
    )


def is_queue_allowed(settings: Settings, queue: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if the queue is reachable under ``TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES``.

    The raising `check_*_access` helpers below and the tools that filter whole
    listings share this one definition of the allow-list.
    """
    return not settings.tracker_limit_queues or queue in settings.tracker_limit_queues

from typing import Annotated, Any

from mcp.server import FastMCP
from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context

from mcp_tracker.mcp.context import AppContext
from mcp_tracker.mcp.params import (
    BoardID,
    BoardPageParam,
    BoardQueueFilter,
    PerPageParam,
)
from mcp_tracker.mcp.tools._access import check_queue_access
from mcp_tracker.mcp.utils import get_yandex_auth, set_non_needed_fields_null
from mcp_tracker.settings import Settings
from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types.boards import (
    Board,
    BoardColumnDetail,
    BoardFieldsEnum,
    Sprint,
    SprintFieldsEnum,
)
from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types.pagination import PaginatedResult

BoardFieldsParam = Annotated[
    list[BoardFieldsEnum] | None,
    Field(
        description="Fields to include in the response. In order to not pollute the "
        "context window - select appropriate fields beforehand. Not specifying fields "
        "will return all available. When looking for a board, id and name are usually "
        "enough; read the full record of the one board you need with `board_get`.",
    ),
]

SprintFieldsParam = Annotated[
    list[SprintFieldsEnum] | None,
    Field(
        description="Fields to include in the response. In order to not pollute the "
        "context window - select appropriate fields beforehand. Not specifying fields "
        "will return all available. Most of the time id, name and status are enough.",
    ),
]


def board_queue_keys(board: Board) -> set[str]:
    """Queue keys a board collects issues from, read off its own auto-filter.

    A board carries no queue field: what lands on it is whatever
    `addFilterSettings` matches, so the queue has to be read out of that filter.
    An inverted condition ("queue is not X") says which queue the board is
    *not* about and is therefore not a match.
    """
    settings = board.autoFilterSettings
    add = settings.addFilterSettings if settings is not None else None
    live = add.liveFilter if add is not None else None
    if live is None or live.fieldValues is None:
        return set()

    keys: set[str] = set()
    for field in live.fieldValues:
        # The captured payloads name this field twice, `id` and `key`, so
        # matching on both keeps this working whichever one a response carries.
        if "queue" not in (field.id, field.key) or field.value is None:
            continue
        for value in field.value:
            fixed = value.fixed
            if value.invert or fixed is None or isinstance(fixed, str):
                continue
            if fixed.key is not None:
                keys.add(fixed.key.upper())

    return keys


def register_board_tools(settings: Settings, mcp: FastMCP[Any]) -> None:
    """Register board and sprint tools (all read-only)."""

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get All Boards",
        description="Get the agile boards (in russian - 'доски') available in Yandex Tracker. "
        "Use the returned board id with the `board_get`, `board_get_columns` and "
        "`board_get_sprints` tools. "
        "Pass `queue` to get only the boards that collect issues of that queue - "
        "that is the way to answer 'which board does this project use'. It matches "
        "the board's own filter, so it misses boards filtering by something else "
        "(personal boards, for one); to catch those, read a few issues of the queue "
        "with `issues_find` and look at their `boards` field. "
        "An organization can have hundreds of boards, so the listing is paginated - "
        "the answer carries `hits` and `pages`, and page 1 is the default. Pass "
        "`fields` to keep the answer small while searching for the board you need. "
        "Boards are organization-wide and are NOT filtered by the server's queue "
        "allow-list: a board's settings can name a queue this server otherwise "
        "refuses to talk about.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def boards_get_all(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        queue: BoardQueueFilter = None,
        fields: BoardFieldsParam = None,
        page: BoardPageParam = 1,
        per_page: PerPageParam = 25,
    ) -> PaginatedResult[Board]:
        # The queue is normalised once and used for both the allow-list check and
        # the match below. Doing it only for the match is what let `queue="dev"`
        # through the check and then answer for `DEV`, and `queue="DEV"` be
        # rejected under a lower-cased allow-list that no other tool honours
        # either (`check_issue_access` reads the key off the issue id as-is).
        wanted = queue.upper() if queue is not None else None
        if wanted is not None:
            check_queue_access(settings, wanted)

        boards = await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.boards_list(
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

        # Tracker has no server-side filter here (`?queue=` is ignored along with
        # `page` / `perPage`), so the queue is matched against each board's own
        # auto-filter. Filtering runs before paging, or `page` would count boards
        # that are then dropped.
        if wanted is not None:
            boards = [b for b in boards if wanted in board_queue_keys(b)]

        # `GET /v3/boards` ignores `page` / `perPage` and always answers with every
        # board, so the paging has to happen here. Left unbounded the tool returns
        # a quarter of a megabyte of JSON on a real organization, which is enough
        # to exhaust the caller's context on a single call - hence a page by
        # default, where the other listings walk themselves.
        if page is None:
            result = PaginatedResult[Board](values=boards)
        else:
            start = (page - 1) * per_page
            # The whole listing is in hand, so unlike the tools paging against
            # Tracker these totals are exact rather than whatever the last page
            # happened to report.
            result = PaginatedResult[Board](
                values=boards[start : start + per_page],
                hits=len(boards),
                pages=math.ceil(len(boards) / per_page),
            )

        if fields is not None:
            set_non_needed_fields_null(result.values, {f.name for f in fields})

        return result

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get Board",
        description="Get a single Yandex Tracker agile board (in russian - 'доска') "
        "with its settings. `autoFilterSettings` is the board's own filter and tells "
        "which issues the board collects - read it to learn which queue a board is about. "
        "Also returns the columns, the field issues are estimated by and the working "
        "calendar the board uses.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def board_get(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        board_id: BoardID,
        fields: BoardFieldsParam = None,
    ) -> Board:
        board = await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.board_get(
            board_id,
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

        if fields is not None:
            set_non_needed_fields_null([board], {f.name for f in fields})

        return board

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get Board Columns",
        description="Get the columns of a Yandex Tracker agile board together with the "
        "issue statuses mapped onto each of them. Use it to find out which status an "
        "issue has to be in to show up in a given column of the board. "
        "Richer than the columns nested in `boards_get_all` / `board_get`, which carry "
        "no statuses.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def board_get_columns(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        board_id: BoardID,
    ) -> list[BoardColumnDetail]:
        return await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.board_get_columns(
            board_id,
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get Board Sprints",
        description="Get all sprints (in russian - 'спринты') of a specific Yandex Tracker agile board. "
        "The currently running sprint is the one with status 'in_progress'. "
        "Use the returned sprint id to put an issue into a sprint "
        "with the `issue_create` or `issue_update` tools.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def board_get_sprints(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        board_id: BoardID,
        fields: SprintFieldsParam = None,
    ) -> list[Sprint]:
        sprints = await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.board_get_sprints(
            board_id,
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

        if fields is not None:
            set_non_needed_fields_null(sprints, {f.name for f in fields})

        return sprints

fix: match the queue allow-lists ignoring case

`is_queue_allowed` and `_is_read_only_queue` compared a queue key to the
configured list exactly, and nothing upper-cases either side: Tracker's
keys are upper-case, the environment variables are written by hand. A
mis-cased entry therefore did not fail, it quietly meant something else -
`TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES=dev` locked out `DEV-1` along with every other
queue, and `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES=dev` left `DEV` writable while the
configuration read as if it were protected. Both now match with
`casefold()`, through one `_listed()` helper so a third list cannot
reintroduce the exact compare.

This is also what `boards_get_all` was working around: the previous
commit passed it `queue.upper()` so its allow-list check would agree with
its own case-insensitive match. That is no longer its business - it hands
`check_queue_access` the queue as the caller spelled it, and upper-cases
only for matching board filters, whose keys `board_queue_keys` reads
upper-cased.

Сделано, `3b1a494`. `task` зелёный: **1381 passed, 1 skipped** (+20).

**`_access.py`** — один хелпер `_listed()` сравнивает через `casefold()`, через него ходят и `is_queue_allowed` (`TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES`), и `_is_read_only_queue` (`TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES`). То есть теперь регистронезависимы обе проверки и для очередей, и для задач — `check_issue_access` берёт ключ из id задачи и идёт в тот же `is_queue_allowed`.

Что это чинит на самом деле: неверный регистр в переменной окружения раньше не падал, а **тихо означал другое**. `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES=dev` закрывал `DEV` вместе со всем остальным — сервер выглядел настроенным, а не отвечал ни на что. `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES=dev` оставлял `DEV` доступной на запись, хотя конфиг читался как «защищена».

**`board.py`** упростился обратно: `check_queue_access(settings, queue)` получает то, что написал вызывающий, а `.upper()` остался только для матча фильтров досок — `board_queue_keys` читает ключи уже заглавными. Костыль из прошлого коммита (`queue.upper()` ради согласия проверки с матчем) больше не нужен.

**Тесты** — новый `TestAllowListsIgnoreCase` в `test_access.py`: матрица «как записано в конфиге × как запросили» по трём регистрам для обоих списков, и отдельно проверка, что очередь вне списка по-прежнему отклоняется (`TrackerError` / `IssueNotFound`) при любом регистре записи.

**Доки** — правило записано один раз там, где его читает оператор: секции `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` в обоих README («`dev` и `DEV` означают одну очередь», с явным упоминанием, что то же и для `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES`). Из карточки `boards_get_all` уточнение про регистр убрал — оно стало свойством всего сервера, а не досок. В `AGENTS.md` — с причиной и требованием ходить через `is_queue_allowed` / `check_*_access`, чтобы третий список не завёл точное сравнение заново.

cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Volumes-Workspace-Projects---ai-mcp-mcp-yandex-tracker/36e49f74-dad6-454f-a436-6c85a7a41e6f/scratchpad/pr46.md <<'EOF'
Closes #42

Sprints could already be passed to `issue_create` / `issue_update`, but there was no way to discover a sprint id. This adds the board layer that was missing — four read-only tools, the protocol/client/caching stack behind them, and a typed link from an issue to the boards it sits on.

The "put this issue into the current sprint" flow now works end to end:

1. `boards_get_all` → find the board (by name, or with `queue`)
2. `board_get_sprints` → pick the sprint with `status == "in_progress"`
3. pass its `id` to `issue_update`

## Tools

| Tool | Endpoint | Docs |
|------|----------|------|
| `boards_get_all` | `GET /v3/boards` | [Получить параметры всех досок](https://yandex.ru/support/tracker/ru/api-ref/boards/get-boards) |
| `board_get` | `GET /v3/boards/{id}` | [Получить параметры доски](https://yandex.ru/support/tracker/ru/api-ref/boards/get-board) |
| `board_get_columns` | `GET /v3/boards/{id}/columns` | [Получить колонки доски](https://yandex.ru/support/tracker/ru/api-ref/boards/get-columns) |
| `board_get_sprints` | `GET /v3/boards/{id}/sprints` | [Получить все спринты доски](https://yandex.ru/support/tracker/ru/api-ref/boards/get-sprints) |

## What the API turned out to be

Most of the design here is a consequence of how `/v3/boards` actually behaves, all of it checked against a real organization (404 boards) rather than the reference:

- **`GET /v3/boards` does not paginate.** `page` / `perPage` are ignored and every board comes back in one response — ~250 KB, enough to exhaust the caller's context in a single tool call. `boards_get_all` slices the list itself.
- **A board has no queue field.** It collects whatever its `autoFilterSettings` matches, so `queue` is answered by reading the queue out of that filter (`?queue=` on the endpoint is ignored too). Boards whose filter names no queue can't be found this way at all — the other route is an issue's own `boards` field, and the server `instructions` tell agents to try both.
- **A filter condition is not always a reference:** `fixed` is an object for most fields but a bare string for enumerated ones like `statusType`, hence `BoardFilterValueRef | str | None`.
- **`/columns` is a different shape** from the columns nested in a board — numeric `id`, `name` instead of `display` — and is the only place the statuses mapped onto a column appear.
- **An issue already carried `boards`**, but unmodelled: `extra="allow"` leaked it into answers while `outputSchema` never mentioned it and `fields` couldn't select it. It's `list[IssueBoardReference]` now, so the id an issue names feeds straight into the board tools.
- **`/sprints` on a non-scrum board answers 400**, not 404 — both need `_raise_for_status` to stay diagnosable, and a board-scoped 404 raises `BoardNotFound`.

## Decisions worth reviewing

**Boards are deliberately not filtered by `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES`.** Post-filtering them by the queues in their auto-filter was the alternative and it takes away what the tools are for: a board has no queue, "the boards of queue X" is already a best-effort match on a filter, and a large share of an organization's boards name no queue at all. So the consequence is documented instead of coded around — a board's settings can name a queue the rest of the server refuses to talk about, and `board_get` and friends answer for any board id. Both READMEs say so where the board tools are described and again where an operator reads about the allow-list. The one check that does apply is on the `queue` argument of `boards_get_all`.

**`boards_get_all` is the one listing that doesn't walk itself.** It answers with the `{values, hits, pages}` envelope like every other listing, but `page` defaults to 1 where the others default to `None` meaning "every page" — the walk costs one request and a quarter of a megabyte of the caller's context. `page: null` is the escape hatch, meant to be paired with a narrow `fields`. `per_page` is 25 rather than 100: a full board record carries `autoFilterSettings` and its columns. Because the whole listing is in hand, `hits` / `pages` are counted locally and exact rather than read off a page Tracker reported.

**Queue allow-lists are now matched ignoring case** (`_listed()` in `_access.py`, both `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` and `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES`, for queue- and issue-scoped checks alike). This is a server-wide change and not strictly board work, but it surfaced here: an exact compare turned a mis-cased entry into a silently wrong policy rather than an error — `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES=dev` locked out `DEV-1` along with every other queue, and `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES=dev` left `DEV` writable while the configuration read as if it were protected.

**Field naming.** `Board` / `Sprint` name their fields as the API does (`createdAt`, `startDate`, …) rather than using `AliasChoices` with snake_case like `Issue` does, so a tool's declared `outputSchema` and the JSON it returns agree on key names. `Queue` / `QueueVersion` are the precedent. One asymmetry the schema can't express is called out in the field description instead: `Sprint.board.id` arrives as a string while the board tools take an int.

**`Sprint.status` is `str | None`, not a `Literal`**, so an unknown future status can't fail validation of the whole response. The four documented values are in the field description and a test covers the pass-through.

## Also in here

- **Server instructions were rewritten** — they still described a read-only server long after 14 write tools had landed, and said nothing about the traps an agent hits first (`version` going stale on its own, templates not being applicable on write, `summonees` being what actually notifies someone, `fields` keeping a listing out of the context window, a missing tool possibly being configuration). `tests/mcp/server/test_instructions.py` now fails if the instructions name a tool that isn't registered or promise an argument a tool doesn't take, which is what let this drift unnoticed.
- Rebased onto 0.8.0 `main`: the board tools were adapted to the reshaped pagination envelope and to `IssueFieldsEnum` being replaced by the free-form `fields` selector.

## Testing

`ruff format`, `ruff check`, `mypy` and `ty` all clean. Full suite **1381 passed, 1 skipped**; 135 of those cover this branch —

- `tests/tracker/custom/boards/` — HTTP layer via `aioresponses`: response parsing, auth headers, empty results, a not-yet-started sprint, status pass-through, and the 400/404 error paths
- `tests/tracker/caching/test_boards_protocol.py` + conformance test
- `tests/mcp/tools/test_board_tools.py` — tools driven through a real `ClientSession`: the `in_progress` lookup scenario, paging and exact totals, `queue` matching (case, inverted conditions, multi-queue boards, filter-before-paging), `fields` trimming, and `BoardNotFound` reaching the caller as an error
- `tests/tracker/proto/test_issue_board_refs.py` — an issue's `boards` is typed, selectable and round-trips under Tracker's own name
- `tests/mcp/tools/test_access.py` — allow-list case-insensitivity across both lists and both check helpers
- `tests/mcp/server/test_instructions.py`, `test_server_creation.py` — instructions stay in sync with the registered tools; all four tools in `READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES`

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_0164YwPL1s8WCkSVBoW18Zmr)_
EOF

refactor: normalise the queue allow-lists once, into a set

The case-insensitive compare landed at the wrong end. `_listed()` walked
the configured list per check, calling `casefold()` on both sides for
every entry - and `is_queue_allowed` is what a listing tool runs per row,
so `queues_get_all` against a long allow-list was doing that work over
and over for an answer that never changes.

`Settings.decode_queue_keys` (was `decode_numbers`, which parsed no
numbers) now returns a `set[str]` of upper-cased keys for both
`TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` and `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES`, so a check is
`queue.upper() in ...` - one hash lookup against a set built once at
load. The validator also accepts a list, set or tuple, so a programmatic
caller is normalised the same way as an environment variable, and entries
differing only in case collapse instead of sitting in the set twice.

`create_test_settings` builds settings with `model_construct`, which
skips validators - it calls `decode_queue_keys` itself now, or the tests
asserting the case-insensitivity would have been asserting it against raw
lists that never went through it.

- `board.py`: Board and sprint tools (read-only)
- **Errors**: use `await self._raise_for_status(response)` instead of `response.raise_for_status()` so Tracker's own `errorMessages` / `errors` end up in the raised `TrackerAPIError` (a bare "Unprocessable Entity" tells the caller nothing). Status codes with an actionable meaning get a dedicated error: 404 → `IssueNotFound` on issue-scoped paths, `QueueNotFound` on queue-scoped ones (`v3/queues/{queue}/...`) and `BoardNotFound` on board-scoped ones (`v3/boards/{board}/...`), 409 on update → `IssueVersionConflict`. git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git log --oneline -1 | cat
fix: match the queue allow-lists ignoring case, from a set

`is_queue_allowed` and `_is_read_only_queue` compared a queue key to the
configured list exactly, and nothing upper-cased either side: Tracker's
keys are upper-case, the environment variables are written by hand. A
mis-cased entry therefore did not fail, it quietly meant something else -
`TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES=dev` locked out `DEV-1` along with every other
queue, and `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES=dev` left `DEV` writable while the
configuration read as if it were protected.

Normalising per comparison would have cost a pass over the list every
time, and `is_queue_allowed` is what a listing tool runs per row. So it
happens once instead: `decode_queue_keys` (was `decode_numbers`, which
parsed no numbers) returns a `set[str]` of upper-cased keys for both
variables, and a check is `queue.upper() in ...`. The validator takes a
list, set or tuple as well as the raw string, so a programmatic caller is
normalised the same way and entries differing only in case collapse.

`create_test_settings` builds settings with `model_construct`, which
skips validators - it calls `decode_queue_keys` itself now, or the tests
would assert the case-insensitivity against raw lists that never went
through it.

Tracker bumps the version on every change, including the queue triggers and automation that fire right after an issue is created, so the version returned by `issue_create` is routinely stale already - re-read it with `issue_get` before retrying, or omit `version` to update the latest version unconditionally.

Templates are read-only helpers: Tracker cannot create an issue or a comment *from* a template, so no write tool takes a template id. Read the template with `issue_template_get` / `comment_template_get` and pass its values as the write tool's own arguments.

To mention or call users on an issue, use the `summonees` argument of `issue_add_comment` / `issue_update_comment` - a plain `@login` in the comment text notifies nobody.

Tools that accept a `fields` argument (`issues_find`, `queues_get_all`, `boards_get_all`, `board_get`, `board_get_sprints`, ...) return only the fields you select. Use it to keep a large listing out of the context window while searching, then re-read the one record you need in full.

The server may be configured to be read-only, or to allow only some queues: a write tool that is missing, a rejected write, or a queue reported as "not found or not allowed" can be that configuration rather than missing data. Say so instead of retrying.

'''

bullet = "- Create and edit issues, comments, worklogs and links (unless the server runs read-only)\n"
assert t.count(bullet) == 1

p.write_text(t); print('ok')

input.command:
git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git log --oneline -1 | cat
feat: agile board and sprint tools

Closes #42

Sprints could already be passed to `issue_create` / `issue_update`, but
nothing could discover a sprint id. Four read-only tools close that:
`boards_get_all` finds the board, `board_get` reads its settings,
`board_get_columns` the columns with the statuses mapped onto them, and
`board_get_sprints` the sprints - pick the one with `status ==
"in_progress"` and pass its id to `issue_update`.

Behind them the usual stack: `BoardsProtocol` with a client and a caching
wrapper, `Board` / `Sprint` / `BoardColumnDetail` and the auto-filter
models, `boards` on `AppContext`, `mcp/tools/board.py`.

Most of the shape here is what `/v3/boards` turned out to be, checked
against an organization with 404 boards rather than against the reference:

- **It does not paginate.** `page` / `perPage` are ignored and every board
  comes back in one response, ~250 KB - enough to exhaust a caller's
  context in one tool call. `boards_get_all` slices locally and takes
  `fields`. It answers with the `PaginatedResult` envelope like every
  other listing, but is the only one that does not walk itself: `page`
  defaults to 1, `page: null` is the escape hatch for the whole list and
  is meant to be paired with a narrow `fields`. Its `hits` / `pages` are
  counted rather than read off a response, so they are exact, and
  `per_page` is 25 because a full board record is not small.
- **A board has no queue field**, so `queue` is matched against the queue
  in the board's own auto-filter (`?queue=` on the endpoint is ignored
  too). Boards whose filter names no queue cannot be found that way at
  all; the second route is an issue's own `boards`, and the server
  instructions tell agents to try both.
- **A filter condition is not always a reference**: `fixed` is an object
  for most fields and a bare string for enumerated ones like `statusType`.
- **`/columns` is a different shape** from the columns nested in a board,
  and is the only place a column's statuses appear.
- **An issue already carried `boards`**, but unmodelled - `extra="allow"`
  leaked it into answers while `outputSchema` never mentioned it and
  `fields` could not select it. It is typed now, so the id an issue names
  feeds straight into these tools.
- **A non-scrum board answers 400 on `/sprints`**, not 404, so both go
  through `_raise_for_status`; a board-scoped 404 raises `BoardNotFound`.

Boards are deliberately left outside `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES`. Filtering the
listing on the queues in each board's filter was the alternative and it
takes away what the tools are for - a board has no queue, "the boards of
queue X" is already a best-effort match, and a large share of an
organization's boards name no queue at all. Only the `queue` argument is
checked. The consequence is documented instead: a board's settings can
name a queue the rest of the server refuses to talk about, so both READMEs
say so where the tools are described and again where an operator reads
about the allow-list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0164YwPL1s8WCkSVBoW18Zmr
EOF

  triggers and automation bump it right after `issue_create`

  id - read the template and pass its values

  configuration rather than missing data, and should be reported as such

`tests/mcp/server/test_instructions.py` fails if the instructions name a
tool that is not registered or promise an argument a tool does not take,
which is what let this drift unnoticed.

```

936884b  feat: agile board and sprint tools                            29 файлов, +2523/-4
b23227c  docs: bring the server instructions up to date with the tools  2 файла,   +100
```

Разбивал по независимости, а не по хронологии — каждый коммит стоит сам по себе и его можно ревьюить или откатить отдельно:

1. **Allow-list'ы** — общесерверное, к доскам отношения не имеет: `settings.py`, `_access.py`, тесты, строки в доках. Поставил первым, потому что доски на этом поведении стоят (тесты `boards_get_all` с разным регистром очереди).
2. **Доски** — весь слой целиком: протокол, клиент, кэш, модели, четыре тула, `IssueBoardReference`, `BoardNotFound`, envelope пагинации, `queue`-фильтр, тесты, README/AGENTS/manifest. Промежуточные метания (сначала голый список → потом envelope; сначала `page=1` без итогов → потом точные `hits`/`pages`) свёрнуты в одно состояние — в истории остался результат, а не путь к нему.
3. **Server instructions** — не про доски: они описывали read-only сервер, когда 14 write-тулов уже были. Отдельно, потому что ценно само по себе, вместе с `test_instructions.py`, который ловит расхождение впредь.

Каждый коммит прогнал отдельно на своём дереве: A — 1273 passed, B — 1374, C — 1386, ruff/mypy/ty чисто на всех трёх. То есть история бисектится, а не только вершина зелёная.

from collections.abc import Iterable
from typing import Any, TypeVar, get_args

from mcp.server.auth.middleware.auth_context import get_access_token
from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context
from pydantic import BaseModel
from starlette.requests import Request

from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.common import YandexAuth

T = TypeVar("T", bound=BaseModel)


def get_yandex_auth(ctx: Context[Any, Any, Request]) -> YandexAuth:
    access_token = get_access_token()
    token = access_token.token if access_token else None

    # Passthrough mode: when MCP OAuth is disabled (no access_token from MCP auth
    # middleware), read the Yandex OAuth token directly from the Authorization
    # header. This enables use behind a reverse proxy that injects per-user
    # tokens (e.g. a gateway that resolves user identity and fetches their
    # stored OAuth token from a secret store).
    if token is None and ctx.request_context.request is not None:
        auth_header = ctx.request_context.request.headers.get("Authorization", "")
        if auth_header.startswith("Bearer "):
            token = auth_header[7:].strip() or None

    auth = YandexAuth(token=token)

    if ctx.request_context.request is not None:
        cloud_org_id = ctx.request_context.request.query_params.get("cloudOrgId")
        org_id = ctx.request_context.request.query_params.get("orgId")

        if cloud_org_id:
            cloud_org_id = cloud_org_id.strip()
            auth.cloud_org_id = cloud_org_id or None

        if org_id:
            org_id = org_id.strip()
            auth.org_id = org_id or None

    return auth


def set_non_needed_fields_null(data: Iterable[T], needed_fields: set[str]) -> None:
    for item in data:
        model_fields = type(item).model_fields
        extra = item.__pydantic_extra__
        # `model_fields_set` is mutated below, so iterate over a snapshot.
        for field in tuple(item.model_fields_set):
            if field in needed_fields:
                continue

            if extra is not None and field in extra:
                # Fields the API returned that the model does not declare
                # (`self`, `id`, `queue`, `boards`, the queue's own
                # `<queue-id>--<key>` fields) live in `__pydantic_extra__`,
                # which carries no `exclude_if=none_excluder`. Nulling one
                # leaves it in the response as an explicit `null`, so dropping
                # it is the only way to honour the field selection.
                del extra[field]
                item.__pydantic_fields_set__.discard(field)
                continue

            field_info = model_fields.get(field)
            # Skip fields whose declared type doesn't allow None (e.g. required
            # `id: int`) - nulling them would produce a response that violates
            # the tool's own output schema.
            if field_info is not None and type(None) not in get_args(
                field_info.annotation
            ):
                continue
            setattr(item, field, None)

class TrackerAPIError(YandexTrackerError):
    """A non-2xx response from the Yandex Tracker API.

    Tracker explains *why* a request was rejected in the response body
    (`errorMessages` / `errors`), which is the only way to tell, for example,
    which field of an issue_create call was invalid. The body is therefore part
    of the raised error instead of being dropped by `raise_for_status()`.
    """

    def __init__(self, *, status: int, method: str, url: str, body: str):
        self.status = status
        self.method = method
        self.url = url
        self.body = body
        self.error_messages, self.errors = _parse_error_body(body)

        details: list[str] = list(self.error_messages)
        details.extend(f"{field}: {message}" for field, message in self.errors.items())
        if not details and body:
            details.append(body[:MAX_ERROR_BODY_LENGTH])

        message = f"Yandex Tracker API error {status} on {method} {url}"
        if details:
            message += ": " + "; ".join(details)
        super().__init__(message)

    """Extract Tracker's `errorMessages` / `errors` from an error response body."""

    """A request to the Yandex Tracker API ran out of its time budget.

    Worth a class of its own only because the alternative is unreadable:
    `str(TimeoutError())` is the empty string, so a timeout reaches the caller
    as `Error executing tool <name>:` with nothing after the colon and no hint
    that time, rather than the request, was the problem.
    """

    def __init__(self, *, method: str, url: str, timeout: float):
        self.method = method
        self.url = url
        self.timeout = timeout
        super().__init__(
            f"Yandex Tracker API request {method} {url} timed out after "
            f"{timeout:g}s. Raise TRACKER_API_TIMEOUT if this endpoint is "
            f"slow for this organization."

async def boards_list(self, *, auth: YandexAuth | None = None) -> list[Board]:
        # This is the one endpoint that hands over an entire organization in a
        # single unpageable response, and it is slow in proportion: 415 boards
        # measured at 7-16s against the 10s default budget, so the call failed
        # on roughly a coin flip. It gets a floor of its own, raised along with
        # TRACKER_API_TIMEOUT when that is set higher.
        timeout = max(self._timeout, BOARDS_LIST_MIN_TIMEOUT)
        try:
            async with self._session.get(
                "v3/boards",
                headers=await self._build_headers(auth),
                timeout=ClientTimeout(total=timeout),
            ) as response:
                await self._raise_for_status(response)
                return BoardList.model_validate_json(await response.read()).root
        except TimeoutError as exc:
            raise TrackerAPITimeout(
                method="GET", url="v3/boards", timeout=timeout
            ) from exc
